title: Caregiver Income Impact & Lost Earnings Estimator
description: Financial cost of unpaid caregiving: direct income loss during the care period, the retirement savings gap from missed 401(k) contributions plus their lost compounding, the cumulative cost of a post-care career setback, and a flagged Social Security reduction estimate, in integer USD cents. The SSA contribution and benefit base and the SSA average annual benefit are selected from a pinned vintage table by an explicit as_of date (the node reads no clock). Ported from ApexLogics display_number #117 (117-caregiver-income-impact, al_id AL-124, CC BY 4.0); DIFFERS-D1..D5 in the porting payload, three modelling constants UNGROUNDED.

as_of.description: Vintage date as YYYY-MM-DD. The node reads no clock; the year selects the pinned SSA table (2025 or 2026) and any other year is REFUSED_UNSUPPORTED_VINTAGE. Must be a real calendar date.

salary_usd.description: Current annual salary in US dollars, at least 0. AINumbers advisory bound 10000-1000000 (the Apex control's min/max); outside the bound the compute still runs and raises ART761_OUT_OF_UI_RANGE_SALARY_USD.

current_age.description: Current age in years. AINumbers advisory bound 18-65 (the Apex control's min/max).

retirement_age.description: Expected retirement age in years. AINumbers advisory bound 55-75 (the Apex control's min/max).

care_years.description: Caregiving duration in years, at least 0. AINumbers advisory bound 0.5-30. A duration that reaches or passes retirement age is allowed and clamps years_after_care at 0.

income_reduction_pct.description: Income reduction during caregiving as a percent, 0-100 (0 = no reduction, 100 = full leave); the compute divides by 100. Refused outside 0-100. 0 is a real value here, not a prompt for the default (DIFFERS-D3).

career_setback_pct.description: Post-care salary setback as a percent, 0-100; the compute divides by 100. Refused outside 0-100. Above 5 adds a credential-offset strategy. The Apex selector offers 0/5/10/20; any number in range is accepted.

contribution_401k_pct.description: Annual 401(k) contribution rate as a percent, 0-100; the compute divides by 100. Refused outside 0-100. AINumbers advisory bound 0-20.

investment_return_pct.description: Annual investment return as a percent, -100 to 100; the compute divides by 100. 0 takes the ordinary-annuity zero-rate branch (fv = pmt * n). AINumbers advisory bound 1-12.

marginal_tax_rate_pct.description: Marginal tax rate as a percent, 0-100. Required because the source dereferences it unconditionally, but it enters NO formula and is echoed with marginal_tax_rate_used=false (DIFFERS-D4). AINumbers advisory bound 10-37.

ss_average_annual_benefit_usd.description: Optional override for the SSA average annual retired-worker benefit in dollars, the same fact as the pinned vintage default (2026: 24864; 2025: 24180). Supply 23000 to reproduce the Apex #117 source constant exactly (DIFFERS-D2); a positive value switches ss_average_benefit_source to user_supplied and raises ART761_SS_AVERAGE_BENEFIT_USER_SUPPLIED.

mcp_tool_definition.name: caregiver_income_impact
mcp_tool_definition.description: Quantify the financial cost of unpaid caregiving from a salary, an age pair and a care duration: direct income loss during the care period, the retirement savings gap from missed 401(k) contributions and lost compounding, the cumulative post-care career-setback cost, and a flagged Social Security reduction estimate, in integer USD cents. as_of selects a pinned SSA vintage (2025 or 2026); the node reads no clock. The SSA term is a flagged linearisation, not the SSA AIME formula.

as_of.description: Vintage date, YYYY-MM-DD; the year selects the pinned SSA table and the node reads no clock.

salary_usd.description: Current annual salary in USD, at least 0.

care_years.description: Caregiving duration in years, at least 0.

marginal_tax_rate_pct.description: Marginal tax rate percent 0-100; echoed, unused (DIFFERS-D4).

ss_average_annual_benefit_usd.description: Optional SSA average annual benefit override in USD; 23000 reproduces the Apex source.

output_schema.description: output_payload: as_of, vintage_year, ss_wage_base_usd, ss_average_annual_benefit_usd, ss_average_benefit_source (pinned_official_<vintage> | user_supplied); the echoed inputs including marginal_tax_rate_pct and marginal_tax_rate_used (always false, DIFFERS-D4); years_to_retirement, years_after_care and years_from_midcare (dead in the source, carried for parity); integer-cent annual_income_loss_cents, direct_income_loss_cents, annual_401k_lost_cents, retirement_savings_gap_cents, career_setback_cost_cents, setback_compounding_rate_bp, ss_reduction_fraction_micro, annual_ss_reduction_cents, ss_lifetime_reduction_cents, total_impact_cents (excl. SS) and total_impact_with_ss_cents; strategies (5 base rows plus one when career_setback_pct > 5); refusals, refusal_reason, domain_errors; caveats (the compliance-flag mirror); scope_note. On refusal every money member is null and refusal_reason names the code.

input_schema_provenance: Top-level properties are exactly the policy_parameters members the kernel reads: as_of, salary_usd, current_age, retirement_age, care_years, income_reduction_pct, career_setback_pct, contribution_401k_pct, investment_return_pct, marginal_tax_rate_pct, plus the optional ss_average_annual_benefit_usd override. Every property type is taken from the compute's read of that member (the nine numerics are arithmetic operands, as_of is the string the ISO comparator and vintage table index). All ten unconditional reads are listed in required, including marginal_tax_rate_pct, which the source dereferences but never uses. The bounds quoted in each description are the Apex control min/max attributes carried over as AINumbers advisory bounds; the hard domain refusals (0-100 percent, care_years >= 0, investment_return_pct within -100..100) are the compute's own guards.
author: PostOakLabs

strategies: Max IRA/401(k) during and after the caregiving period - even small contributions compound over the years left to retirement
Consider spousal IRA contributions where applicable (allows retirement savings with little or no own income)
Negotiate phased re-entry or remote arrangements to limit the career setback
A written caregiver agreement with family for shared caregiving can provide modest taxable income and keep the Social Security record alive
Review employer EAP, FMLA and caregiver benefits BEFORE reducing hours
Invest in a credential or certification during or after caregiving to offset the 10% setback (see the AINumbers workforce ROI node)
output_example.scope_note: Not a benefit projection and not tax advice. The Social Security term is a flagged linearisation (ART761_SS_ESTIMATE_MODELED), not the SSA AIME formula - use art-282-social-security-claiming-optimizer or pf-139-social-security-bridge for a real benefit estimate. The career-setback compounding rate, the caregiving-year divisor, the 15 percent cap and the 20-year draw are modelling constants carried from the source, each UNGROUNDED. marginal_tax_rate_pct is accepted and echoed but enters no formula (source DIFFERS-D4: the Apex page reads it and never uses it). No inflation, no FMLA/state leave value, no unpaid-care opportunity cost beyond the direct wage loss, no employer-benefit valuation.
